name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection

summary.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is the Department of Homeland Security agency responsible for border security and customs enforcement. On this site it appears as a customer of Anduril Industries, whose autonomous surveillance towers CBP designated a program of record in July 2020 with plans for up to 200 towers under a five-year contract whose value was not disclosed, and of Palantir Technologies, whose role in CBP's Analytical Framework for Intelligence (AFI), a system that assigns risk-assessment scores to travelers, was uncovered by the Electronic Privacy Information Center through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit.

sources.title: CBP taps Anduril for virtual border sentinel system
CBP Plans to Exempt Social Media Data from Legal Protections

facts.claim: In July 2020 CBP declared Anduril's autonomous surveillance tower system a program of record, moving it from a research and development effort to a budget line item, with plans to deploy up to 200 autonomous surveillance towers; FedScoop reported the designation granted Anduril a five-year project.
facts.quote: CBP declared a relatively new border security surveillance tower system a program of record, which moved it from a research and development effort to a line item in the budget

sources.title: CBP taps Anduril for virtual border sentinel system
CBP Makes Autonomous Surveillance Tower System Program of Record
Anduril Sentry towers get CBP program-of-record status

facts.claim: The value of the five-year Anduril tower contract was not disclosed; Anduril executives told The Washington Post it would be several hundred million dollars. Defense Daily reported CBP's plans for extensive deployment of autonomous surveillance towers on the southern border.
facts.quote: it is not known how much the five-year contract is worth, though Anduril executives told the Washington Post it would be several hundred million dollars

sources.title: Anduril raises $200m, wins contract for autonomous surveillance towers along US-Mexico border
CBP Plans Extensive Deployment of Autonomous Surveillance Towers on Southern Border

facts.claim: An investigation reported that deaths of border crossers occurred within the advertised detection range of nearly two-thirds of the Anduril towers it analysed; Anduril responded that proximity does not prove a missed detection.
facts.quote: Anduril responded that proximity does not prove a missed detection

sources.title: Investigation finds more than 110 deaths within range of Anduril border towers

facts.claim: The Electronic Privacy Information Center reports that CBP's Analytical Framework for Intelligence assigns risk-assessment scores to travelers, and that EPIC uncovered Palantir's role in the system through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit; in 2017 CBP proposed to exempt social-media data in the system from Privacy Act protections.
facts.quote: CBP Plans to Exempt Social Media Data from Legal Protections

sources.title: CBP Plans to Exempt Social Media Data from Legal Protections

facts.claim: Wired reporting relayed by The Motley Fool described a five-year DHS blanket purchase agreement with Palantir allowing agencies including CBP and ICE to make purchases of up to $1 billion without the normal competitive bidding process; this is a department-wide ceiling, not a CBP-specific award value.
facts.quote: allows agencies, including Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), to bypass the normal competitive bidding process for purchases of up to $1 billion

openQuestions: Site claim (Deep State): 'Anduril Industries Lattice OS contracts and Autonomous Surveillance Towers (AST) deployed along domestic borders' is supported in substance by the 2020 program-of-record reporting; the anduril file additionally records a $363 million Extended Range Sentry Tower award and 300 towers deployed by late 2024, which were not re-verified here.
Site claim (Deep State): the 'ICE ImmigrationOS ($30M no-bid sole source award)' concerns ICE, not CBP, and was not checked here.

No cbp.gov page, USAspending record or FPDS entry was opened; the Palantir AFI award value and the Anduril contract value remain undocumented. A DHS Privacy Impact Assessment for AFI would be the primary source for Palantir's role.
The Runtime investigation into deaths near Anduril towers is a single secondary source; its methodology and date were not examined.
The web search budget was exhausted before cbp.gov and USAspending could be searched.
